props.title: Miracle Mile
props.initialSlug: The end is near, run for your life.

sections.content: Miracle Mile stands as one of the most unique apocalyptic thrillers ever made, unfolding in real-time during one frantic Los Angeles night. Director Steve De Jarnatt crafted a masterpiece of escalating tension that begins as a sweet romance between Anthony Edwards and Mare Winningham, then transforms into a desperate race against time when Edwards accidentally intercepts a phone call warning of incoming nuclear missiles. The film's brilliant use of its Wilshire Boulevard location creates a microcosm of society breaking down, while Tangerine Dream's pulsing electronic score amplifies the mounting dread. It shares DNA with other Reagan-era nuclear anxiety films like The Day After (1983) and Testament (1983), but its intimate scale and noir-tinged atmosphere set it apart.

sections.content: The film's influence can be traced through later apocalyptic thrillers that mix personal stories with global catastrophe. Seeking a Friend for the End of the World (2012) echoes its romantic elements against doom, while These Final Hours (2013) mirrors its real-time urgency. The way Miracle Mile uses its LA location - particularly the iconic La Brea Tar Pits - creates a symbolic backdrop about extinction and survival that later films like Volcano (1997) would attempt to replicate.

What sets Miracle Mile apart is its masterful tonal control, shifting from romantic comedy to paranoid thriller to existential horror. The film's technical achievements, including several complex tracking shots through the Art Deco corridors of the Miracle Mile district, influenced later single-night thrillers like After Hours (1985) and Good Time (2017). Its use of pay phones and late-night diners creates a distinctly analog apocalypse that feels both dated and timeless. SUBHEAD: Nuclear Anxiety in Reagan-Era Cinema

sections.content: The film emerged during a vital period of atomic-age cinema that included War Games (1983) and The Manhattan Project (1986). Unlike those films' focus on prevention, Miracle Mile deals with the helplessness of ordinary citizens caught in geopolitical crossfire. Its influence extends to modern disaster films like Greenland (2020), though few match its intimate scale and emotional impact.
